_comment: EXAMPLE incident records for the recall scorer. 'observed' is the set of symbols that actually broke, as triaged by a human -- this is the input the engine cannot produce for itself, which is exactly why the comparison is worth making. The change_id values below point at rows in data/recall_fixture_ledger.jsonl, which is committed precisely so these numbers reproduce on a clean checkout. The live ledger (data/audit_ledger.jsonl) is runtime state and is deliberately untracked, so it is NOT what these examples are scored against. INC-003 deliberately names a change with no recorded decision, to exercise the NO_BASELINE path.

incidents.summary: Baseline case. The approved decision for MR-118 covered 'append', and 'append' is what broke. The prediction held.

Same release, but the blast-radius engine broke too. MR-118's recorded decision covered only 'append', so compute_blast_radius is a missed prediction. This is the finding the module exists to surface: something broke that no recorded decision had predicted.

No decision was ever recorded under MR-999, so there is nothing to score against. Must report NO_BASELINE rather than a clean bill of health, because 'we could not check' and 'we checked and were right' must never look the same.
